points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree (a tree in which each node has at most two children). Equivalent wording such as 'a tree where each node has up to two children' earns the mark.

States the ordering property: for any node, its left child is smaller than the node and the node is smaller than its right child. Equivalent wording, such as 'left subtree values are less than the node and right subtree values are greater', earns the mark. The answer must give the ordering in the correct direction (left smaller, right larger).

rubric.notes: A full answer names the structure as a binary tree and gives the ordering rule with smaller values on the left and larger on the right, for any node. A partial answer gives only one of these ideas, or reverses the direction. An answer that omits both, or describes something else, earns no marks.
